Low raking amber hard from port side, gold burning the crests while deep teal pools the troughs; one blown white specular rides the leader's crown.
Backlight from astern rims every hull in hot brass, the forward faces dropping into ox-blood shadow; a bright line scores the very top of each swell.
Light driving through the water from the far end, the shallow enamel bottom glowing amber below the fleet, the hulls standing dark against that burning ground.
A single warm source high and off to starboard bleeds cadmium yellow across the near surface; the far water falls away into cold blue-grey dark.
Cold blue-white overcast owns the whole field except one ox-blood hull, the only warm body in frame; its wet crown carries the single hard specular.
Green-gold light bouncing up off the bright enamel through the bright enamel below, teal shadow pressing down from overhead; the underside of every hull unreadable.
Hard light driving through thick gold fog so the fog itself is the lit body; the water beneath goes indigo, hulls dark as standing stones inside it.
Flat cool grey owns the surface except one crest catching a break of hot yellow; the troughs either side go almost black against it.
Candle-coloured light raking from one side, cobalt shadow answering from the other; one hard specular blazes flat white on the leader's crown.
Moonlight-cold silver rides every crest at exactly the same angle; deep in the troughs warm amber lies pooled and still where the cold cannot reach.
Dawn light low and rose from the far end, foam lit pink on its lit face and slate on the shadow face; the water between hulls holds both colours at once.
Light having passed through the curved skin of one bubble throws a small bright rose patch onto a hull's flank; the surrounding surface stays cool teal.
Hard top-light directly overhead, every hull casting a sharp black shadow on the bright enamel below; the crests between hulls blown white, the troughs going dark.
One narrow band of hot amber light lies across the water exactly where the fleet is running; everything forward and aft of that band drops into cold indigo dark.
Deep green deep in the water body, brass-coloured light skimming only the very peaks of the swell; the flanks of every hull below the waterline invisible.
Cold cyan owns the whole field; one amber reflection has stretched and is wobbling its way across it, crossed by the hull that made it.
Low hard light from astern skims the surface at almost zero degrees, every crest catching gold and every trough sinking to near-black; the rear hull is half-erased in the blaze.
Backlight raking through the surface from the far end makes the thin crests translucent rose-amber at their edges; the hulls interrupt it as dense black forms.
Overhead source slightly off-centre pours cadmium yellow onto the port side of every hull; the starboard flanks answer in cold slate, the bottom between them lit and pale.
Hard cold top-light flattens every trough to a dark mirror reflecting indigo; the crests catch it as blown white lines, the hulls between them in amber shadow.
Low amber from one side catches only the uppermost millimetre of each crest, turning them brass; deep teal fills everything below that line, including all the hull sides.
Backlight from astern so acute that spray particles travelling upward are individually lit in gold against the indigo the water becomes in their shadow.
One concentrated warm source high and central throws cadmium yellow straight down, the bright enamel bottom bouncing green-gold back up; the hulls are lit from both above and below at once.
Cold blue-white from high and flat, the surface a grey field, until the leading hull's wet chrome cap catches the whole source and returns it as one hard white specular.
Rose light low from the far end crosses the full length of the water, the near troughs holding amber deep inside them while the far crests glow cadmium at the tip.
